newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES, GILDER TIED FOR LEAD AT RAIN-MARRED KAPALUA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES, GILDER TIED FOR LEAD AT RAIN-MARRED KAPALUA.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and former tournament champion Bob Gilder were tied for the lead Friday after second-round play was suspended due to darkness at the $1.1 million Kapalua International.

Jones and Gilder both shot two-under-par rounds of 69 at the Bay Course, one of two courses being used for this unofficial PGA event. They were tied at 11 under par through 36 holes and led Fred Couples, Davis Love III, Billy Mayfair and Paul Stankowski, who were tied at 10-under.

Play was delayed by rain for nearly two hours early in the afternoon and later was suspended due to darkness with 12 of the 56 players still on the course. They will complete their second rounds Saturday morning.
Peter Jacobsen and Scott McCarron were tied at nine-under 135. Jacobsen shot four-under 69 at the Plantation Course, while McCarron had a three-under 68 at the Bay Course.
Woody Austin, Mike Hulbert and Briton Sandy Lyle were three shots back at eight under par.
The Kapalua International is not a sanctioned PGA event and the top five players on the PGA money list skipped it, as did 20-year-old sensation Tiger Woods.
The Plantation Course is a par-73 layout that measures 7,263 yards. The Bay Course is a par-71, 6,600-yard layout. Each player plays two rounds on each course.
